record.paper_title: Exploring Progressions: A Collection of Problems
record.original_question: Determine every possible common difference d of an arithmetic progression whose first term is a1 = 6 and which has both 62 and 104 among its terms.

evidence.quote: Determine the difference of each arithmetic progression which has first term a1 = 6 and contains the numbers 62 and 104 as its terms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An arithmetic progression is a sequence (a_n)_{n≥1} of real numbers of the form a_n = a_1 + (n-1)d, where a_1 is the first term and d is the common difference. We say a number x is a term of the progression if x = a_n for some positive integer n.

Find all possible values of the common difference d of an arithmetic progression with first term a_1 = 6 such that both 62 and 104 appear as terms of the progression. (Assume d is a positive real number; describe the complete set of admissible d.)
artifact.status_search_result: This is a standard elementary exercise. The condition that 62 and 104 are terms of the progression with a_1 = 6 forces d to divide both 62 - 6 = 56 and 104 - 6 = 98, so d must be a positive common divisor of gcd(56, 98) = 14. Restricting to positive integer differences yields d ∈ {1, 2, 7, 14}.

status_evidence.title: Elementary computation
status_evidence.claim: The admissible positive integer common differences are exactly the positive divisors of 14.
